paragraphs: At the next rehearsal, the violinist asked the section to try the same short passage from two seating positions. They noticed that hearing the neighboring part was harder from the far end of the row. Rather than immediately asking for more volume, they discussed which line needed to be heard at that moment. They also recorded the passage and listened together.

The recording did not tell them where to put every chair, but it gave them another way to check the balance. When the piano returned, the players tried to keep listening across the group. The useful change was therefore not simply a new seat. It was a habit of checking what they could hear and adjusting their choices with other players.
rationale: 関係節・間接疑問・不定詞・比較を読み、具体的な練習から注意の向け方の変化を推論する。

paragraphs: As the basket became better known, Lena checked it carefully each morning for scarves that needed washing or repair. She asked customers to leave damaged items in a separate bag so they would not be offered to the next person. Making help easy to use still required care behind the scenes. When the basket was empty, a note explained that more scarves were needed, without asking anyone to describe their finances. Customers could respond to the need without learning who had taken the earlier items. Lena also made space for anonymous suggestions about the arrangement. She wanted to notice practical problems while keeping a person's use of the basket separate from a public judgment about whether that person deserved help.

paragraphs: Before making the next piece, Jin asked a colleague to imagine cleaning it in a small room. She pointed out that reaching one fitting would require turning the whole object over. Jin changed the panel's position and tested whether it could be removed with an ordinary tool.

He kept a note of the test and explained which parts would still need professional attention. Designing for future use did not mean promising that a customer could repair everything alone. It meant noticing likely tasks and making their limits clear. The sales photograph still mattered, but it was now only one part of the explanation. Jin wanted the customer to understand how the object could be cared for after the photograph had been forgotten.
rationale: 間接疑問・動名詞・関係節・受動態を読み、使用後の手入れと修理の限界まで考える設計を推論する。

paragraphs: After the exhibition, the student sorted the visitors' comments into observations, questions, and suggestions. She did not treat every proposed change as a decision that had already been made. Some ideas conflicted with one another, and several needed more information about the people who would use the hall. She tested the narrow corner again and noted which arrangements left enough space for the wheelchair figure. The model helped her compare routes, but could not show every difficulty of moving through a real building. She therefore planned to discuss the design with people who had relevant experience. The conversations had extended the project beyond its first presentation. They had also shown why an inviting model was a starting point for investigation rather than a complete test of access.

paragraphs: Before the new season, the coach asked players privately which parts of practice they found difficult to ask about in front of the team. He explained that the question was about improving the sessions, not selecting players for matches. Some wanted a chance to repeat a movement slowly; others needed help understanding an instruction.

The coach kept the usual team practice and added a short period for these questions. He checked later whether players felt able to use it. A place on the schedule alone did not mean that asking had become easy. The second card had drawn his attention to quiet support, but he did not assume that every player needed the same kind. Listening again was part of putting that lesson into practice.
